title: A member of Henrietta Maria's household (Paris) to Charles I, January 1646, in Lasry's SP106-8 key: TNA SP 106/10 ff. 235-236 (DECODE R924)

steps.what: Fetched the DECODE record page of R924 with the shared cookie; it links Pettersson's transcription, Lasry's reconstructed key 'TNA SP106-8' and his plaintext of ff. 235-236 and 238-240 (2020-10-23).

Re-fetched the record files and applied the key group by group to the 2012 groups of ff. 235-236 (apply_key.py): 1850 get a value; on the lines whose columns line up in Lasry's interlinear file (1604 keyed groups) every value equals his plaintext. 162 groups have no value in the key (58 distinct three-digit numbers, 11 low figures).

Split from the former combined target hm1645 under the one-key rule (George Lasry, 14 Oct 2026): R924 is the only letter of the six in the SP106-8 key. Folder, profile, page and ledgers separated; the earlier step is kept as recorded.
Full texts listed in outcome.texts (George Lasry's request of 22 Oct 2026): linked the DECODE record holding Pettersson's transcription and Lasry's plaintext; no local copy

Reading audit, per-document pass (George Lasry's sentence test): Lasry's plaintext of R924 is on DECODE only (git-ignored copy in no checkout); nothing could be read. Relabelled decoded, not read; class already solved kept (Lasry's decipherment); fraction_read 0.9195 -> 0.

Re-read b35: DECODE R924 fetched with the project cookie (2 images, Pettersson's transcription, Lasry's key, plaintext and interlinear, now in decode/, git-ignored); neighbours R922, R923, R925, R926 and R788 opened: cipher only, no decipherment or clear copy.

Found that Eric Sams deciphered this letter and the Queen's of the same key in 1976 for Ian Roy (Archivaria 21, 1985-86, pp. 89-90: a number cipher in Cowley's hand, two letters to Charles I, Jermyn in English and Henrietta Maria in French, January 1646, PRO); his solution is not printed. Jermyn to Nicholas, 26 Jan 1646 (SP 106/10 no. 15) refers to 'the kinge his letters' on the Portugal embassy and marriage: this letter. Writer: Henry Jermyn.

Decoded afresh with Lasry's key; low unvalued figures read as nulls; date 'Ian. 26' and '5 or 6 thousand' read as numerals in clear; codes 168 hope, 116 can, 334 what, 227 new adopted by sense at every occurrence (flagged); R924_reading.md and R924_en.md written, aligned word by word with the decode (three modernised spellings restored). Score 0.545 plain, 0.649 explicit holes; marked read, grade B.

Verify sweep (reading audit v2): R924 reading re-scored with the 16 words that rest on the four sense-valued codes (168 hope, 116 can, 334 what, 227 new) as holes (research/reading_audit/v2_score.py): 0.649 -> 0.597 (46/77) explicit holes, 0.545 -> 0.494 plain; the same 0.597 without 227, which Lasry's plaintext carries. Under the bar; demoted to decoded, not read, fraction_read 0. Class already solved kept (Lasry's decipherment on DECODE).

George Lasry gave permission on 24 Oct 2026 to use his DECODE decryptions with attribution: his plaintext file D3090 saved verbatim with an attribution header as lasry/R924_decryption.txt; credit added to R924_reading.md and R924_en.md; read_share re-measured on the reading (v10_relabel.measure); state read in part.

outcome.method_basis: The letter was taken from George Lasry's plaintext on the DECODE record (23 Oct 2020); his SP106-8 key, applied here only as a check, reproduces it.
outcome.fraction_read_source: 23 Oct 2026, re-read b35: the one document, R924 (2012 groups), reads (R924_reading.md); 2012/2012 = 1.0 by document. 85 code tokens inside it stay open. 23 Oct 2026, verify sweep v2: R924 back to decoded, not read (0.597 with its four sense-valued codes counted as holes); 0 of 1 documents read.

gaps.item: three-digit word-list numbers with no value (58 distinct, 85 tokens: 324, 428, 321, 532, 208, 797 ...)
gaps.detail: Lasry's key lacks them; Eric Sams's 1976 solution is unprinted (Bodleian / Ian Roy papers). Four valued here by sense (R924_reread_log.md). Verify sweep 23 Oct 2026: the four sense-valued codes (168 hope 7x, 116 can 5x, 334 what 2x, 227 new 2x; Lasry has hold, brought, -, new) counted as holes put the reading at 0.597, so the letter is decoded, not read.

gaps.item: Eric Sams's decipherment of this letter (1976)
gaps.detail: filed in the Bodleian per his letter to R. A. Sayce, 9 Oct 1976; not online

outcome.notes: Lasry's key and decipherment on DECODE (2020) are the basis of the reading. DECODE's start date (26 June 1646) does not fit the letter's own 'Paris Jan'; queued as a correction. 22 Oct 2026, reading audit: no text of the letter was in the repository; decoded, not read. 23 Oct 2026, re-read b35: Lasry's files fetched, the letter decoded afresh and read (R924_reading.md, grade B, four code values by sense). Eric Sams deciphered this letter in 1976 (Archivaria 21, 1985-86, pp. 89-90: Jermyn to Charles I, January 1646), unprinted; writer Henry Jermyn. Class kept: Lasry's decipherment exists on DECODE (2020).

credits.note: reconstructed key 'TNA SP106-8' (Jan 1646) and interlinear plaintext of R924, with dating notes; George Lasry (decryption on DECODE, used with his permission, 24 Oct 2026)

texts.label: R924, Paris, January 1646
texts.summary: A writer at Paris to Charles I against Sir H. Compton's journey and the treaty for Prince Charles's marriage with Portugal, on Montreuil's mission, the frost that stopped the river traffic, and levies of five or six thousand men to send over.
texts.note: 24 Oct 2026: George Lasry gave permission on 24 Oct 2026 to use his DECODE decryptions with attribution; his plaintext is saved verbatim (lasry/R924_decryption.txt) and credited on the reading and English. read_share measured on R924_reading.md (v10): coherent but under the 95% bar, so read in part; 85 code tokens (58 distinct) his key lacks are the holes; four sense-valued codes count as holes.

reading_review.note: Reading built from the figures with Lasry's key and checked against his decryption on DECODE R924 (D3090, now saved verbatim as lasry/R924_decryption.txt with his permission, 24 Oct 2026); coherent sentences; 85 code tokens (58 distinct) his key lacks are the holes; four sense-valued codes count as holes.
